Subject: Infra capacity checkpoint: QBR prep & unit-econ asks

Team —

As we slot the infra section of the QBR (next Tues leadership block), I need a concise set of asks and the supporting numbers by EOD Friday so I can synthesize. High level: we need a single slide that says where runway is (Q3 spend + forecast), what levers we can pull (batching, cache, quantization), and the estimated impact in unit economics and latency at P95.

Please provide the following by Friday 18:00 PT:
- Current committed GPU pool (slots & device types) + utilization in the last 30d (avg and 95th percentile).
- Q3 actual GPU spend to date and projected Q4 baseline if we do nothing.
- A conservative and optimistic estimate for token unit cost change if we: (a) increase avg batch size from 8 -> 16 with our work-conserving scheduler, (b) deploy prefix/KV caching for common prompts (hit rate assumptions: 10%, 25%, 40%), and (c) switch 2/3 of batch-inference to INT8 quant profile. Please include assumptions.
- Any procurement timing constraints (ProcureCorp) that would affect adding reserved capacity before EOY.

Markus — can you attach the most recent capacity model and the simulation of batching outcomes? Neha — can you run a quick cache-hit sensitivity (sheet attached to your inbox). Priyom — add runway / SKU mapping so we know which products map to which pools.

Minimal prose. Bullet numbers we can paste into the slide. I will merge and send to execs for pre-read.

Thanks —
Lauren

On Wed, 12 Sep 2028 at 09:15, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> ...

Quick reply — attaching two artifacts: the capacity model (CSV) and a short PDF with the batching sims I ran against the 30-day trace. TL;DR up front:
- Current committed pool: 48x A100s (40 active slots), 24x H100 burst nodes. Avg utilization (30d): 68%. 95th percentile utilization: 92% during peak windows.
- Q3 YTD GPU spend: $1.18M. Baseline Q4 (no changes): ~$1.35M (growth and seasonal load baked in).
- Batching sims (current avg batch size 8 -> target 16): median per-token latency up by ~6% but P95 improves by 11ms (due to better GPU amortization). Estimated token cost reduction: 16% (conservative) to 25% (optimistic) depending on tail flattening.
- Prefix/KV caching: at 10% hit -> ~4% token cost reduction; 25% -> ~10% reduction; 40% -> ~15% reduction. There is a memory+eviction tradeoff; results in batching-sim-results.pdf.
- INT8 path: for 70% of requests we can use INT8 without quality regression in our eval set, giving additional ~18% compute cost saving on those requests. Overall combined (batching + 25% cache + INT8 for 70%) -> ~38% unit cost reduction in best-practice stack; realistic plan is to target ~22% in first pass.

Attachments: batching-sim-results.pdf, prefix-cache-hitrate-breakdown.xls

Open questions I flagged in the PDF:
1) Work-conserving scheduler requires a small infra change (1 week dev + 2-week ramp) — should be fine for Q4 rollout if we prioritize.
2) Cache eviction policy needs product input: which prompts to prioritize (we included product tags in the sheet).
3) Procurement: if we need more reserved A100s to flatten P95, procurement lead time is ~6 weeks.

-Markus

- Levers & expected impact (first-pass numbers): batching (8->16): ~16% cost down; prefix cache @25%: ~10% additional; INT8 on 70%: ~18% additional (stacked -> ~22% realistic).

- Ops timeline: work-conserving scheduler (1w dev + 2w ramp), cache pilot (2w pilot), INT8 serve profile phased with evals (3w). Procurement: new reserved cards needs 4-7w lead time per ProcureCorp.
